map.Lessons 5-1, 5-2 & 5-3 — areas of parall: Lessons 5-1, 5-2 & 5-3. Areas of parallelograms, triangles, and trapezoids. Four reader gates stand before a real plan.
map.Previously: the crew woke me in the Obse: Last time: the crew woke me up. Their Brightside plan just won the job. Now they have to draw it.
map.Previously, in Axiom City: the crew woke: Last time, in Axiom City: the crew woke VEX. Then they beat every builder in town. Now they get to fix up the Brightside lot. First the sketch must become a floor plan. It needs REAL sizes.
map.Survey sketches in, floor plan out. One: Sketches in. Floor plan out. One week. Draw each shape. Make each number true.
map.Hargrove & Sons, \"site support.\" Don't: Hargrove & Sons, "site help." Do not mind me. Or my tape measure.
map.That's Fenwick — the surveyor from the l: That's Fenwick. He worked for the team that lost. He has measured our gate three times. He got three answers. None of them ours.
map.Hargrove & Sons lost the bid — but they': Hargrove & Sons lost the job. But they still price it. They hope the council picks their "cheap" numbers.
map.First shape on the plan: the dance floor: First shape on the plan: the dance floor. The sketch shows a parallelogram. It is like a rectangle that leans.
map.Slanted floor? You bill by the SLANTY si: Slanted floor? You charge by the SLANTY side. Long side, big job. Trust me.
map.Incorrect protocol. A parallelogram is a: Wrong. A parallelogram is a pushed-over rectangle. Cut the slanted end off. Slide it across. Area = base × height. The height stands PERPENDICULAR to the base. Like a flagpole. Slanted edges are fakes.
map.Perpendicular means meeting at a right a: Perpendicular means they meet at a right angle. Mina's test sketch: base 5 m, height 3 m → 5 × 3 = 15 m². The slanted side is not in the math.
map.Reader — ink the dance floor's true area: Reader, find the dance floor's true area. Fenwick keeps patting the slanted side. Don't let him.
map.The dance floor is a parallelogram: base: The dance floor is a parallelogram: base 9 m, height 6 m. Fenwick keeps pointing at a slanted side. Find the TRUE area in square meters.
map.Conceptual: a parallelogram is a pushed-: Conceptual: a parallelogram is a pushed-over rectangle. Cut the slanted end off. Slide it across. Nothing is cut in half. The slanted edge is not the height.
map.Procedural: multiply the base by the hei: Procedural: multiply the base by the height. The height meets the base at a RIGHT angle. It is the dashed line. It stands straight up. Do not use the slanted side.
Shade over the stage corner. It is a triangle. Fenwick just priced cloth for the WHOLE parallelogram.
map.Fabric comes in rectangles! Buy it all!: Cloth comes in rectangles! Buy it all! Hargrove deal!
map.Two copies of that canopy snap together: Two of that triangle fit into one parallelogram. We only sew ONE of them. So do base × height. Then take half.
map.Noah's whiteboard check: a triangle with: Noah's board check: a triangle with base 4 m and height 6 m → 4 × 6 = 24. Half of that is 12 m². A triangle is half its parallelogram. Always.
map.Reader — cut the canopy order. Half the: Reader, cut the cloth order. Half the parallelogram. All of the shade.
map.The stage's shade canopy is a triangle:: The shade over the stage is a triangle: base 12 m, height 5 m. How many square meters of cloth does it need?
map.Conceptual: two copies of the canopy wou: Conceptual: two of the shade cloths fit into a parallelogram. You only sew ONE of them.
map.Procedural: multiply base × height first: Procedural: multiply base × height first. Then divide that by 2.
map.Seating terrace. The bench rows shrink t: The seats. The rows of benches get shorter near the stage. Short base in front. Long base by the garden.
map.A trapezoid: one pair of parallel sides: A trapezoid has one pair of parallel sides: base one and base two. Its true width is their AVERAGE. Add the bases. Divide by two. Multiply by the height. Both bases count. Always both.
map.Mina's sketchpad check: bases 4 m and 6: Mina's check: bases 4 m and 6 m. Their average is 5. Times height 2 → 10 m². A rectangle in between, dressed as a trapezoid.
map.Reader — average the bases and ink the t: Reader, average the bases. Find the seat area. Each stone counts.
map.The seating terrace is a trapezoid: para: The seats sit on a trapezoid. One parallel base is 6 m (by the stage). The other is 10 m (by the garden). It has a height of 4 m. Find the REAL square meters of stone.
map.Conceptual: a trapezoid acts like an in-: Conceptual: a trapezoid is like a rectangle in between. Take the short base and the long base. Its true width is their AVERAGE. Both bases count.
map.Procedural: follow the scaffold (b₁ + b₂: Procedural: follow the steps (b₁ + b₂) ÷ 2 × h. Add the two bases. Divide by 2. THEN multiply by the height.
map.Thursday. A rival quote lands on the cou: Thursday. The other team sends a price to the council. Shiny paper. Bad math.
map.Forty?! The reader measured that terrace: Forty?! The reader measured those seats. Their "cheap" price comes from a bent tape measure.
map.Distortion source: located. If the counc: I found the glitch. Say the council buys a fake number. Then the stones run out halfway. Our plan: finish the REAL floor plan. Show just how Fenwick bent it.
map.Council review at nine tomorrow. We stil: The council meets at nine tomorrow. The plan still needs a mural wall. It needs a banner too. And we must answer Hargrove's forty.
map.Reader inks the numbers. I'll hold the r: Reader writes the numbers. I hold the ruler. No one touch my pencil.
map.Boss Gate: finish the floor plan — two a: Boss Gate: finish the floor plan. Find two areas. Show one fake number.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. The plan must be: BOSS GATE. Three locks. The plan must be real by morning. Every square meter of it.
map.Council review at nine. Three locks stan: The council meets at nine. Three locks stand before a stamped floor plan:
map.Hargrove's quote prices the terrace at 4: Hargrove's price says the seats need 40 m² of stone. What did they do wrong?
map.Conceptual: every shape keeps its own ru: Conceptual: each shape has its own rule. A parallelogram stays whole: base × height. A triangle takes half. A trapezoid averages its two bases first.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 is base × height. Loc: Procedural: Lock 1 is base × height. Lock 2 is base × height ÷ 2. Lock 3: redo the seats with the trapezoid rule from Gate 3. Which one mistake gives just Hargrove's number?
map.Approved. Every shape true, every meter: Yes. Each shape is true. Each meter is ours. Fenwick's tape measure got a new job.
map.Next quest: the planters. Soil doesn't c: Next job: the plant beds. Soil does not come in squares. It comes in CUBES. Whole truckloads of them.
map.Parallelogram.A pushed-over rectangle. A: Parallelogram.A rectangle pushed over. Area = base × height. The height must be PERPENDICULAR to the base. Slanted sides are fakes.
map.Trapezoid.One pair of parallel bases. Av: Trapezoid.One pair of parallel bases. Find their average: (b₁ + b₂) ÷ 2. Then multiply by the height. Both bases count.
map.Fenwick's tricks.Billing the slant, skip: Fenwick's tricks.He used the slant. He skipped the half. He used one base. Each fake area is a real formula. One step is bent.
map.\"A floor plan is a promise drawn to sca: "A floor plan is a promise drawn to scale. Measure like you mean to keep it." — A.V.
map.completed Unit 5 · Episode 1: Floor Plan: did Unit 5 · Episode 1: Floor Plans. You can find areas of parallelograms, triangles, and trapezoids.
map.Episode 2 — Solid Ground — is waiting at: Next is Episode 2, Solid Ground. It waits at the plant beds.
map.Mina's practice sketch: a parallelogram: Mina's sketch: a parallelogram path. Base 7 m, height 4 m, slanted side 5 m.
map.Area = base × height = 7 × 4 = 28 m². Th: Area = base × height = 7 × 4 = 28 m². The 5 m slant is not in the math.
map.Proof by scissors: cut the slanted trian: Proof with scissors. Cut the slanted triangle off one end. Slide it to the other end. You get a 7 × 4 rectangle. Same 28.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.Noah's test pennant for the gatepost: ba: Noah's test flag for the gate: base 6 m, height 9 m.
map.The pennant is half of that: 54 ÷ 2 = 27: The flag is half of that: 54 ÷ 2 = 27 m² of cloth.
map.Valeria's pocket sketch: a trapezoid ram: Valeria's sketch: a trapezoid ramp pad. Bases 5 m and 9 m, height 2 m.
map.Area = 7 × 2 = 14 m². A rectangle 7 m wi: Area = 7 × 2 = 14 m². A rectangle 7 m wide would cover the same ground.
map.A trapezoid has bases 3 m and 5 m and he: A trapezoid has bases 3 m and 5 m. Its height is 4 m. Area in m²?
map.Practice plan, different numbers: a mura: Test plan, new numbers: a mural wall parallelogram 6 m long, 2 m high → 6 × 2 = 12 m². No halves. No slants.
map.A side-door banner triangle, base 4 m, h: A banner triangle, base 4 m, height 3 m → 4 × 3 ÷ 2 = 6 m².
map.A fake quote prices a trapezoid (bases 3: A fake price says a trapezoid is 14 m². Its bases are 3 m and 7 m. Its height is 2 m. Real area: (3 + 7) ÷ 2 × 2 = 10. The faker used just one base, 7 × 2. He did not average. Same trick, small lie.
map.A mural wall is a parallelogram with bas: A mural wall is a parallelogram. Its base is 7 m. Its height is 2 m. Area in m²?
map.9 × 6 = 54 m² — the whole floor, slant i: 9 × 6 = 54 m². The whole floor. No slant. Fenwick is wrong. Done!
map.You halved it — but this isn't a triangl: You took half. But this is not a triangle! Cut and slide keeps a parallelogram WHOLE.
map.That's 9 × the 7 m slant. The height mus: That is 9 × the 7 m slant. The height must be PERPENDICULAR to the base. Use the dashed line.
map.Base × the perpendicular height — the da: Do base × the perpendicular height. Use the dashed line. Not the slanted edge.
map.12 × 5 ÷ 2 = 30 m². Half the parallelogr: 12 × 5 ÷ 2 = 30 m². Half the parallelogram. All of the shade. The cloth is ordered.
map.That buys the WHOLE parallelogram of can: That buys cloth for the WHOLE parallelogram. That is Fenwick's price. The shade is half of it. One more step.
map.Base × height first… then remember what: Do base × height first. Then think: a triangle is half of what?
map.(6 + 10) ÷ 2 × 4 = 32 m². Both bases vot: (6 + 10) ÷ 2 × 4 = 32 m². Both bases counted. Keep this number in mind. Someone is about to get it wrong on purpose.
map.That's ONE base × the height — only the: That is ONE base × the height. Only the garden side counted. A trapezoid averages BOTH bases first.
map.Add the two bases, halve the sum, then m: Add the two bases. Cut the sum in half. Then multiply by the height.
map.Lock 1 holds. You halved the mural wall: Lock 1 holds. You took half of the mural wall. A parallelogram stays WHOLE at base × height.
map.Lock 1 holds. The mural wall is a parall: Lock 1 holds. The mural wall is a parallelogram. Multiply its base by its height.
map.Lock 2 holds. That's the full parallelog: Lock 2 holds. That is the full parallelogram of cloth. The triangle is HALF of it.
map.Lock 2 holds. Banner = base × height ÷ 2: Lock 2 holds. Banner = base × height ÷ 2. Decimals multiply just like whole numbers.
map.Lock 3 waits. Tap the mistake hiding ins: Lock 3 waits. Tap the mistake in Hargrove's 40.
map.Lock 3 holds. You proved the terrace you: Lock 3 holds. You found the seat area at Gate 3. It was NOT 40. Hargrove made the stone bill too big.
map.Lock 3 holds. The terrace is a trapezoid: Lock 3 holds. The seats are a trapezoid. There is no triangle to halve. Make 40 from the seat numbers.
map.Lock 3 holds. No slant is even listed fo: Lock 3 holds. No slant is given for the seats. Which one number, times the height, makes just 40?
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. Mural 42 m², banner 18 m: ALL LOCKS OPEN. Mural 42 m². Banner 18 m². Hargrove's 40 is a fake: one base × height. He skipped the average. The floor plan is REAL.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
